hero_dek: Every day, fresh science from arXiv becomes text anyone can read. Here's how it all works — before you dive in.
whatis_lead: Every day arXiv — the largest open library of new science — publishes hundreds of papers. We take their full text, hand it to an AI, and ask for one honest thing: explain it clearly. Not shorter, not louder — just clear.
whatis_muted: Every article comes out in several languages and at four depths. All free, non-commercial, forever. We adapt a paper only when its license allows it.
depth_intro: Not "short" and "full", but a ladder. Start wherever you're comfortable and go deeper if it grabs you. The depth switch sits at the top of every article.
rung1_when: When the topic is new and you want to grasp the essence without jargon. Any jargon here is always spelled out.
rung2_desc: Once science already draws you in.
rung2_when: A lively account with intuition and imagery. The default level — every article opens here.
rung3_desc: With formulas and the story of the discovery.
rung3_when: Closest to the original. For those who want depth and aren't afraid of math.
rung4_when: One thought, like a post in a feed. To decide whether to read on.
map_intro: Left to right — from the feed to a living map of knowledge. The logo always brings you home.
map_main: A feed of articles by day. An endless stream grouped by date — like a news feed for science.
map_tags: Concepts. Topics in physics (black holes, dark matter…). Click for every article on the topic plus its explanation.
map_laws: Laws and principles. The "house of formulas" — laws, theorems, effects. A formula is only a rendering; the meaning is in the text.
map_scientists: Scientists. The great minds behind the discoveries — with a biography and related topics.
map_sections: arXiv sections. Cosmology, exoplanets, high-energy physics… — a filter by field.
map_authors: Authors. Researchers who publish on arXiv. An A–Z index, with tag chips beside each name.
map_graph: The knowledge graph. Tags ⇄ laws ⇄ scientists and all their links. You can wander through knowledge, not just read it.
map_fav: Favorites. Articles you've marked with a heart, gathered in one place.
langs_intro: The language switch is in the row under the menu. Russian is the source language; the rest are prepared by AI.
langs_note: The Arabic version is complete, with a right-to-left (RTL) layout: the same frontier science, in the same plain words. The architecture doesn't cap the number of languages — a new one is added without rewriting the site.
search_h2: Three ways to find what you need
search_intro: The 🔍 button in the header searches everything at once: articles, concepts, laws, scientists and sections — just type a word. The prefixes remain for those used to them, and now merely narrow the view:
search_examples: For example, #black_hole — articles on the topic, @Hawking — by author, !Einstein — linked to a scientist. Next to it, the 📅 Calendar: year → month → day — jump back to any date. And the sections filter narrows the feed to the arXiv fields you want.
graph_h2: Wander through knowledge, don't just read it
graph_p: Every article links to topics; topics link to laws and scientists; scientists link back to topics. It's one knowledge graph. On any tag, law, or scientist page there's a mini-map of its surroundings — with a depth dial + / −. And on the graph page — the whole map at once, with filters and search across all three types.
graph_note: The practical point: you came for one article about neutron stars — and left understanding how they connect to general relativity, to the effect that describes it, and to the people who discovered it.
tiles_kicker: Nice things to know along the way
tile1_s: Toggles and remembers — read whichever way is easy on the eyes.
tile2_s: A short intro to the site — opens on click.
tile3_s: Every article has an honest estimate of how long it takes.
tile4_s: Real figures and plots from the PDF, with captions, plus an AI cover.
tile5_s: Mark an article or leave a short note — no sign-up.
tile6_s: The button at the bottom takes you onward, not back to the feed.
foot_tag: science in plain words · for everyone · free
contact_cadence: For now we cover the top 10 papers a day, with a focus on physics. Next comes the full stream, unfiltered.
contact_authors: Are you an author? Write to us from the address listed in your paper and we'll correct the summary.
contact_write: Liked it, or didn't — tell us:
contact_adapt: The project can be adapted to a concrete need: connect new sources where their licence allows it, add a language, tune the selection to a given field. Proposals go to proposal@bridge42worlds.academy.
submit_p: You can send your paper directly to article@bridge42worlds.academy. We check it with AI: whether it is novel and whether it fits a section. If it does, the work may be published here in our processed form. Please format it to the usual standards. We reply either way, and it is free.
submit_note: Submitted work must carry the same licence we use ourselves: CC BY 4.0.
contact_free: Cooperation with educational institutions is entirely free. We are glad to take your wishes and requirements into account: add new sources, or adapt the feed to your programme, as far as our resources allow. Very specific tasks may also call for your own help with the development, under open-source licences.
contact_join: Would you like to take part in the project? Write to admin@bridge42worlds.academy.
submit_scope: We do not limit ourselves to particular sources. Coursework by university or school students is welcome too. Only two things matter: the work must meet the standards expected of scientific writing, and it must relate to physics or engineering.
express_p: Some articles are marked “express” — a quick take built from the author’s abstract only, without parsing the full paper. Full articles are written from the whole text: context, methods, results, formulas — deeper and more detailed. Express can be hidden from the menu, leaving only full ones.
an_h2: See the whole project at once
an_p: Beyond individual articles there is a bird’s-eye view: the project map — a 3D cloud of everything we’ve covered. A dot is an article, nearby dots share topics, colour marks a topic group the algorithm found on its own. Group names and descriptions are written by AI, in plain words.
an_tabs: The map has four views: Articles — the cloud of works; Authors — every researcher we processed, along an “experimentalist ↔ theorist” axis; Fly — fly through the cloud and open articles like stars; Heat — a 3D landscape of “topic × month”.
an_dash: The Dashboard holds the numbers: articles per day and month, which fields of science are covered, what people read, plus how many papers exist in the open arXiv archive and how much of it we have covered so far.
an_note: All of it is computed from our own data, without any external service.
map_learn: The course. A knowledge tree: 14 topics of three paragraphs each, every one with an interactive stand, a worked-through formula and a hit-the-target challenge. Alongside it: a retrospective of discoveries, a reference of formulas and constants, maths made plain, and bold hypotheses.
search_meaning: Search has two modes. By words — instant and offline: matches titles and concepts. By meaning — the query goes to the server and is compared against the meaning of the articles themselves: “why is the sky blue” finds the article on light scattering even if those words never appear in it. Meaning search works across all languages at once: ask in Arabic and it will find English articles, answering with Arabic titles. While it thinks, a fact or a short question from our own articles appears instead of empty space.
tutor_p: In the course every paragraph comes with someone to ask: put it in your own words — “where does that factor of two come from?”, “what is this for in practice?” — and get an answer about this very material, not a generic one. The bot sees the paragraph text and the formulas right beside you.
tutor_wait: Answers to quizzes and challenges earn points, and points add up to ranks — from Curious to Academician. The ladder is borrowed from the real one: observer, lab assistant, graduate, PhD, doctor of science. For now it all lives in your browser; once sign-in exists, the score can be carried over.
tutor_note: The bot has a daily allowance of questions — it calls a paid model, and the allowance keeps the section from running dry. An ordinary reader will only hit it on a very long evening.
council_hint: The project has an observers' council — a small circle of readers who decide where it goes. We do not invite by page count: invitations go to those whose remarks are visibly to the point, and first of all to authors of the papers we covered. If that speaks to you — write to us, the door will be found.
name_why: About the name. bridge42worlds reads as bridge for two worlds — the world of science and the world of a person outside it. A bridge is genuinely needed there: a paper clear to ten specialists stays invisible to everyone else. The digits standing in for “for two” are a quiet nod to The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, nothing more. We do not have forty-two worlds. There is one world, and it is ours.
authors_hint: For authors. Want your paper covered? We adapt works under open licences (CC BY). If yours carries the default arXiv licence, upload a new version with a licence change and do write to us at article@bridge42worlds.academy with the paper id: an author's letter puts it at the top of the queue. Details on the authors page.
